description: Galvanised steel crowd-control barrier panel of vertical tube bars in a rectangular frame, on two flat swivel feet, with hook-and-eye ends for linking.

image.prompt:
Product photograph of one isolated object, shot from a HIGH THREE-QUARTER ANGLE: the camera is well above the object and tilted down about 30 degrees, so the top of the object is clearly visible along with its front and one side. Not a straight-on elevation.

The object: Galvanised steel crowd control barrier, a rectangular tubular frame filled with closely spaced vertical round bars, a flat bridge foot at each end set square to the panel, a hook on one end and an eye on the other for linking to the next panel Materials: Dull galvanised zinc with white oxide bloom, rust at every weld, scuffed feet.

Form: build the object from a few simple, chunky, closed volumes. Prefer solid panels over lattice, mesh, grilles or perforated screens; keep any openings few, large and clearly separated. No thin spindly protrusions, no wires, no chains, no fringes, no lace, no fine filigree, no dense repeated slots or cut-outs. Keep the silhouette simple and readable from every side. Keep the object's SHAPE simple; richness must come from the surface finish, wear and materials rather than from intricate geometry. The object is still photoreal and highly detailed in its texture -- only its form is simple.

Framing: long-lens near-orthographic perspective, minimal foreshortening. The object is perfectly centred and occupies about 75% of the frame height, with clear empty margin on all four sides. The whole object is in frame; nothing is cropped.

Background: completely flat seamless neutral 50% grey (#808080). The object floats in empty space against an infinite seamless backdrop, photographed as a cut-out with nothing underneath it. There is no surface for it to rest on and nothing for it to cast a shadow onto. No floor, no ground plane, no horizon line, no cast shadow, no contact shadow, no reflection, no vignette, no gradient.

Lighting: flat even studio illumination from all sides, soft and shadowless, like a lightbox. No strong key light, no rim light, no coloured light, no specular blowout, no dramatic highlights. Colours must read as true albedo.

One object only, nothing else in frame. No people, no hands, no other props, no packaging, no text, no labels, no watermarks, no measurement annotations, no arrows, no borders, no drop shadow.

Photoreal, sharp focus edge to edge, clean and undamaged geometry, realistic materials and surface wear. Not stylised, not cartoon, not low-poly, not a 3D render preview, not a wireframe.

license.notice: Fully synthetic. No third-party scanned or scraped geometry.

review.critique: FINAL VERDICT. Overall visual fidelity 0.93. 1,924/4,000 triangles, 3/4 draw calls, 1/3 materials, 3/6 unique geometries, one 1024 px canvas at 5.3 MB built in 109 ms. Open frame: turntable run with --allow-holes on the _holecc measurement; collapse ratio from the declared depth.

featureReviews.evidence: Envelope 2.03 x 1.10 x 0.55 m built to the DECLARED 2.00 x 1.10 aspect (1.82 H) against the proxy's foreshortened 1.33 H; band table |delta depth| 0.0175 H. The 0.12 m top corners are a SWEPT polyline with one mitred ring per point -- the first build chained a cylinder per segment, each extended by 1.2 r to close its joints, and a 0.038 m corner chord against a 0.025 m overlap rendered the bend as an accordion of pleats. The leg structure is re-read off the plate's +X end, where the crown, the ground and the rail are all legible at one x (0.001669 m/px): uprights and bars dying into a bottom rail at 0.30 m, two stubs at +-0.67 into centred feet, against the first build's uprights run to the ground with the feet under them.
featureReviews.notes: Width residual is the declared aspect; arithmetic in the spec. The plate's -X end contradicts its +X end on the legs and the +X reading is built.

featureReviews.evidence: Five sheeted bays and one open bay at the fifth position as the plate shows (the proxy read two open). Each is now a PRESSED PAN rather than a flat plate: a 13 mm returned rim extruded z -0.007..+0.006 over a face recessed to z -0.005..-0.001, the face overlapping the rim opening by 7 mm rather than meeting its reveal. The rim's shadow line is what the plate shows in every bay. 8 mm clear of every tube; check-coplanar clean at 1 mm.

Flat 0.55 m feet on stubs at +-0.67, an eye ring on -X, and two hook brackets on +X at 0.53 and 0.885 m by the plate's own vertical scale. The brackets are PRESSED FLAT STRAP with the broad face turned out, not the 0.011 m tube of the first build, which shaded to a narrow highlight and read as wire. Twelve conical weld beads straddle the rail SURFACE at the plate's measured rust tone (#826e58, the mean over the 2.2% of the frame with R-B > 26); the first build put ten flat 42 x 20 mm boxes at the rail's CENTRELINE, where a 28 mm flare on a 21 mm rail poked clean out of it and rendered as bronze washers threaded onto the bars.
featureReviews.notes: Every joint radius is differentiated -- rail 0.0231 fatter than the 0.021 uprights that die into it, stubs 0.0164 thinner than the rail -- so no two meeting tubes are tangent.

featureReviews.evidence: MEASURED against the plate over matched flat panel crops. Plate: mean luma 157-159, sd 12-16, p5..p95 139..181. First build: mean 142, sd 8-10, span 21, and CLIPPED at the top (p75 = p95 = 147 -- the grime tile did nothing over the upper half of the panel). This build: mean 157/163/158, sd 12.2/11.5/7.5, p5..p95 137..179. A new hot-dip zinc tile carries drift, CLUSTERED spangle, fine 1-2 px grain, scratches, drip streaks and rust bled from the ground and crown bands; the tile is a multiply map authored about mid 0.98 with every albedo divided by the measured 0.64 transfer, so the surface varies in BOTH directions about its mean instead of only downward.
featureReviews.notes: Two crops with the same histogram can look nothing alike: the grain and scratch layer was added on a matched-magnification comparison, not on sd. The right-hand crop's 7.5 is the narrow end panel seen near edge-on.
